explanation: Represent work as (node, subtreesTraversed) stack entries. Push a marked copy of the current node, then its right child, then its left child. LIFO order makes both subtrees finish before the marked node is emitted.
timeComplexity: O(n+1): each node creates a constant number of stack actions and is emitted once.
spaceComplexity: O(h+1) auxiliary pending-action stack for tree height h, plus O(n) returned values. Worst-case h=n.

correctness: The stack records the remaining traversal actions in reverse execution order. Expanding a node schedules exactly left subtree, right subtree, root, because the most recently pushed action runs first. A marked entry emits its value once instead of expanding again; null entries do nothing. Each real node is expanded and emitted once, so exhausting the stack returns every value in the required order.
walkthrough: For the tree with root 8, left child 4 (whose right child is 6), and right child 10, finish 6 before emitting 4, then finish 10, and only then emit 8. Result: [6,4,10,8]. The explicit marked entry delays each emission until its scheduled turn.
edgeCases: An empty tree returns an empty list.
Repeated values are emitted once per node; do not deduplicate.
A skewed tree has height n, so pending-stack space can be linear.
